column1: # canon_reads.tsv - every file a paper generator reads through a canon root (R1 P3 F7, W1-CANON).
# The contract an M canon (/work/canon_m, config/r1/paths_aws_m.yaml) must satisfy: the producers
# (F3/F4/F26/F19/N5/F21) write the 'product' rows under the October basenames, the final job's
# assembler lays them out and copies the 'carried' rows from October, and `tools/r1_canon.py check
# ROOT` must print CANON_OK before any generator runs. tests/test_r1_canon_generators.py proves that
# the files each Python generator opens under the canon roots are exactly its rows.
#   generator  analysis/paper/<script> (or tools/compare_all.py) that reads the file
#   key        a canon key (cal frames expected raw_verified paper_inputs cal_intermediates) - the row
#              lives in the canon at <prefix>/<rel> and its October source is canon.october_path(key, rel);
#              or another paths.yaml key (legacy_v2_output legacy_multiplex fwci repo_root): read in
#              place, never copied, listed so F24' can show the numbers it feeds as not recomputed
#              or canon_root: a file at the canon root beside the six key folders (a canon tree only;
#              tools/r1_canon.py check covers the six keys, not this)
#   rel        path under the key's root; may hold fnmatch wildcards (* ?) - check needs >= 1 match
#   kind       product  - written by an M stage; the canon must carry it (CANON_FAIL if absent)
#              carried  - no M producer; the assembler copies the October file unchanged
#              optional - a product the M job may omit (F19 cut it, or F20 is out of scope by the
#                         author's ruling of 2026-10-15); the generator skips its block in M
#   reason     the producer, or why the file is carried / optional
# MANIFEST.sha256 files and CANON.json are infrastructure and are not rows.
